title: 1951 AHSME Problem 16
statement: If in applying the quadratic formula to a quadratic equation \[ f(x)=ax^2+bx+c=0, \] it happens that \(c=\dfrac{b^2}{4a},\) then the graph of \(y=f(x)\) will certainly:

solutions.text:
The condition gives \[ b^2-4ac=b^2-4a\left(\frac{b^2}{4a}\right)=0. \] Hence the quadratic has a repeated real root, so its parabola is tangent to the \(x\)-axis.

Thus, the correct answer is C.
hints: Substitute the condition into the discriminant \(b^2-4ac\)
A quadratic with one repeated real root touches the horizontal axis once
